result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=with, B=without): A recommends one clear option, Source Sans 3, explains the licensing accurately, and is honest that Georgia and Calibri can't be assumed on Android. It also asks for a test print and a check on an old phone, though it doesn't mention a library computer. B is useful and covers web and print sizing well, but it offers several choices instead of one. Its serif fallback stack includes Charter and Georgia without saying these are missing on Android, and its only test is to block the font rather than check real devices or a print. | pass 2 (A=without, B=with): B gives one concrete open-licensed family for both web and print, explains PDF embedding, and suggests checking the license on the project's own page. It is also explicit about which named fonts Android doesn't ship. A offers more options and good sizing advice, but its serif stack names Charter and Georgia without saying older Android lacks them, and its only testing advice is to block the font. B asks for a test print and a check on an old phone, though it never says to test on a library computer.
